steps.content:
EDGE-05: The mobilization order failed to pass, as expected, but the margin was surprisingly wide.
EDGE-05: The "incident" at the Eastside peace ball a few days ago might be the cause. Ms. Andohar's little stunt sent quite a shock through the council.
EDGE-03: It's fine. 04 and Nirvana suffered too heavy a loss; they needed this concession. Besides, FAC's reserves are sufficient. We never planned on counting on them for this war anyway.
EDGE-03: What's the status on SHP-13? I heard there's a new development.

EDGE-07: You heard right! And it's a big one. Totally unexpected.
EDGE-07: Long story short, an <color=#fb9259>anomalous Mania contaminant</color> slipped through every one of MBCC's defenses, made direct contact with SHP-13, and... nothing happened. No incidents.

EDGE-07: It's confirmed that the contaminant's Mania profile now shows a blended signature—parts of BR-005, traces of MBCC-S-098, even echoes of SHP-13's own shackles—all in a bizarre, stable harmony. We've got an invaluable sample on our hands!
EDGE-07: This means even without live data from the Third Observatorium on BR-005, we now have a whole new way to track and analyze its condition!

EDGE-02: Hmm, quite fascinating indeed.
EDGE-02: So, was it that little Sinner's excessive longing for the Shepherd that pulled BR-005 all the way to DisCity? Or did the Black Ring use her as a conduit, and now as bait, trying to lure our Shepherd out...?

EDGE-02: ...I'm getting ahead of myself. Too much speculation. My apologies. For now, we observe. Closely.
EDGE-02: Its presence will undoubtedly affect SHP-13. Monitor him. Ensure he doesn't lose control.
steps.female_content:
EDGE-02: ...I'm getting ahead of myself. Too much speculation. My apologies. For now, we observe. Closely.
EDGE-02: Its presence will undoubtedly affect SHP-13. Monitor her. Ensure she doesn't lose control.

steps.content:
EDGE-07: What about 01? Any progress? Will he be ready in time?
EDGE-07: Are we drawing too much attention? Could they detect us...
EDGE-02: With his record, no news is good news. We wait and buy him time. As for detection...
EDGE-02: With our adorable Shepherd in play, I doubt it'll be an issue.
EDGE-02: Now then, let's continue observation and documentation. This war will yield very interesting data, it seems.
[Reception Room]

August 2, N.F. 115 13:00
MBCC Chief's Office
Using "city-state security" as a pretext, the newly appointed Speaker, Max King, had arranged this meeting to grant himself a formal meeting with the MBCC Chief.

Public speculation is that his failed mobilization order has dealt a severe blow to his authority, pushing him to recruit allies. But now... he's clearly unhappy, just not for the reason everyone thinks.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...You're just going to keep talking to me like this?
Absolutely cheerful, you greet him with a smile and a gesture toward the seat.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Speaker King, it's good to see you. It's been a while. How are things at the council?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I heard about the struggle to get that security funding through. The mobilization order failing... that's a tough break. With all that pressure and everyone watching, just let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And don't worry, we're completely alone here. No prying eyes or ears. You can speak freely.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Free? It was anything but free! I've had to invent excuses and dodge half the city just to be here! Do you know how worried I've been since the Great Expo?! So can you please, for once, be serious?

steps.speaker: Option
options: Hmm? But I am being serious.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: You call this being serious?!
With a flourish, he produces a mirror from God-knows-where. Held within its glass, your reflection gazes back—rosy-cheeked and radiant, seated at your desk as if touched by a sudden, glorious light.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Wait, what the ****! Is this place haunted for real? Why can't the mirror show it?!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I mean, what in the world is that attached to you? It's seriously creeping me out. Is this some kind of Mania contamination?
[Phantom Hella's portrait, hanging from Chief's neck]
You are utterly stunned by his words.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I'm not blind! Hey, wait a second! Did she just give me the finger?! I can't make out her expression, but there's no mistaking that!!
The Speaker's frustration mounts to a hilariously animated degree, coaxing a cheerful laugh from you in return.
As an ordinary person, Max King has never been able to see Hecate's Mania Nightmare. The fact that he can see Hella fills you with a giddy joy, as if her presence has become tangibly real.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's perfect. I've been wanting to introduce you.
Right on cue, the shadow at your neck peels away. It spirals through the air before landing dramatically on the desk, striking a theatrical pose to match your announcement.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Her name is Hella. She's from Syndicate, and, like Hecate, she was one of the first Sinners I met.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even now, as a phantom, I'm sure she's still deeply connected to her real self. If she's appearing like this, it has to be for a reason. Something important. That's why I've been trying to communicate with her. Max, can you hear her speaking?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's a real shame you can't. Hella's famous for her sweet words. She's Syndicate's Ambassador of Civility, absolutely brilliant at making people smile. I know you'd like her.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Wait, are you seriously showing off your "daughter" to me right now?!
A few minutes later, Max King rubs his reddened hand from pounding the table. He slumps onto a nearby sofa in resignation, sprawling out ungracefully as he scratches his head.
Good grief... He actually came to discuss serious matters with him. After all that commotion, any semblance of a serious atmosphere has completely evaporated.
steps.female_content: Good grief... He actually came to discuss serious matters with her. After all that commotion, any semblance of a serious atmosphere has completely evaporated.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Okay, seriously, what is your deal with Catherine Augustus?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: The drama she caused at that "anti-war" ball? She grabbed every single headline. Now I've got everyone asking me whether the Andohars are planning a coup, or if DisCorps is making a move. And—

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: She was there as your plus-one, wasn't she? The whole city's buzzing with rumors.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In a way, it's a collaboration.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She needs a backchannel into city security, and I need her troops. After Adelaide stripped me of my power, seeking support elsewhere was my only real option.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Honestly, I don't believe she's truly against the mobilization order. My guess is... she sabotaged it last time because she had too many restrictions placed on her. Wasn't happy about being held on a tight leash.
Finally feeling clear-headed? Max King can't help but be amazed by the magic of a good mood.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Is working with DisCorps really the right move?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Look, I haven't seen war firsthand, but I know this much: you won't be fighting Mania monsters or some Underground lunatics there.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Those Outlanders... just a month ago at the Great Expo, you were running yourself ragged trying to protect them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You think I'm not ready for a war? Worried that I can't handle it?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I'm worried about you.
He turns the mirror toward you once more.
In the mirror, you see only yourself sitting at the desk, revealing the truth that Hella isn't actually by your side.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I'm afraid that weight will crush you. It's because you have a good heart. And people with good hearts pay a double toll on a place like that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Call someone "good" or "bad" these days, and all I hear is which side they're on. But I don't have the luxury to dwell on it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For me right now, objectives matter more than stance. A month ago, my job was to ensure the Great Expo ran smoothly. Today, it's bringing Hella home. And I'll do that, no matter what it takes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll do anything to get it done. If I do nothing, if there's nothing I can do... that's the real pain.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm not lost, Max. You don't need to worry.

He opens his mouth to speak, but the words are stolen by the sudden vibration of his phone. A message from his secretary: Time to return. The unspoken warning is clear—he can't linger too long. Someone is watching.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Alright, duty calls. Can't keep the whole cabinet waiting. Please, take care of yourself. And I mean it, if you need anything, just say the word.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Just don't spend all your time with your little girl. Remember, you've got friends. Real, living people who've got your back. Alright?

options: Of course, Speaker. Your orders are my command.

steps.content: He scoffs at your joke, but seems relieved that you still have the energy to crack wise.
His smile in return is genuine, though it doesn't quite reach his eyes; relief is there, but so is a shadow of the worry that came before.
[Scene Change] Corridor
Exiting the Chief's office, Max King is immediately met by two young girls flanking the doorway—Hecate and Elvira, looking like stern sentinels.
He offers a terse nod and steps aside, a silent invitation. Hecate seizes it, slipping past him into the office to find her Chief.
Elvira remains. Falling into step beside Max King, she matches his pace down the corridor, their conversation a hushed, urgent stream of words.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: The mobilization order's future is in doubt. While the Sillage Society has been quieter since the Euphoria incident, the public's resistance against war is far stronger than I ever expected.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: And now, this sensationalist garbage about ${PlayerName} and Augustus? It's blatant propaganda, likely funded by the Outlands. What a mess.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ......I can imagine how it must be.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But because of Jele... because I was close to an Outland spy, the 9th Agency doesn't trust me anymore. They've questioned me a few times, and now they watch what I can see. I don't have access to much information now... so I'm afraid I can't be of much help. I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: It's okay. Just having you here is a tremendous help.
He turns around to look back. They've rounded a corner in the hallway, but from here he can still see ${PlayerName}'s office. The door remains firmly shut.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: My hands are tied. I can't visit often, and even out there, I'm buried in endless chatter, most of it useless. It's frustrating. To be constantly worried but unable to act.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: That's why it's so reassuring knowing there's a smart cookie like you by his side. I'm counting on you, Miss Genius Stewart. Look after my buddy for me.
steps.female_content: That's why it's so reassuring knowing there's a smart cookie like you by her side. I'm counting on you, Miss Genius Stewart. Look after my girl for me.

steps.content: "Since when is the Chief your buddy?" Elvira wants to retort, but she manages to hold her tongue.
steps.female_content: "Since when is the Chief your girl?" Elvira wants to retort, but she manages to hold her tongue.

steps.content: Because now, everyone is in the same boat.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...I'll... do my best.
[Scene Change] Back to Isolation Cell
[Scene Change] (a cool mansion with cold color tones)

steps.speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
steps.content: ...That smell... That sound... The Outlands' dogs, right nearby, lurking, plotting... The Outlands' dogs are coming...

steps.speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
steps.content: Blood for blood... Blood for blood... General... lead us to battle, let our blades drink deep of the Outlanders' blood...

The woman removes her final piece of jewelry, hangs her sword with deliberate care, and lowers the needle onto the record. As a gentle melody fills the room, it blunts the edges of the whispers at her ears, making "them" sound less gloomy.
The phone rings. She sees the number, and her entire face lights up.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hello? So after standing me up at the ball, you finally decided to pick up the phone yourself? Go on, I'm listening. This better be good.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Oh. I see. So your little friend's back. You must be thrilled. How is she?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hmm? Not the real one? There's a copy now? Hahaha, since when did the new era's Mania become so creative? This Black Ring really knows how to put on a show.
Her tone softens.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Are you going to look for her? You must be short-handed.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Fine. They're yours. Broken Blade Squad 3 is under your command now. Bring that kid home safe, and make it a clean victory.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Take care of my soldiers. They're the best you'll ever get.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I'll be waiting for good news.
The call ends, but the smile it brought remains, still lingering on her lips when her deputy enters the room.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Look at that. All that fire and enthusiasm. You always see it in the rookies.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Broken Blade Squad 3 is your most reliable unit. You're just handing them off to an outsider?

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: ${PlayerName} lacks proper military training and doesn't seem to fully trust you.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Well, I see talent, and I allow for stubbornness. I did the same with every one of you.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Now, let's see what he's truly capable of... Our focus must be on preparation. The time is almost upon us.
steps.female_content: Now, let's see what she's truly capable of... Our focus must be on preparation. The time is almost upon us.
